concept: Apple Platform Frontier for Mac Utilities
summary: Source-anchored research for Apple Platform Frontier for Mac Utilities. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: asc (rorkai/App-Store-Connect-CLI) is an MIT-licensed, unofficial Go CLI: asc validate, submit, asc review status/doctor, asc status --watch; authenticates with key-id, issuer-id and private key, with --bypass-keychain for headless CI. It states it is not affiliated with Apple. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

Review submission via API is a three-step flow: POST /v1/reviewSubmissions (app + platform), POST /v1/reviewSubmissionItems linking the app version, then PATCH the submission with submitted=true. Order matters; out-of-order calls give 422/foreign-key errors. (medium confidence)

Availability is not guaranteed: SystemLanguageModel.default.availability returns .available or .unavailable with reasons deviceNotEligible, appleIntelligenceNotEnabled or modelNotReady, and Apple tells developers to check it before creating a LanguageModelSession and show a fallback. A Mac App Store diagnosis feature must therefore degrade to non-AI output on ineligible Macs or when the user has Apple Intelligence off. (high confidence)

WWDC26 introduces a LanguageModel protocol so session code is unchanged when swapping the Apple model for a third-party one (Anthropic and Google publish Swift packages; open-source CoreAILanguageModel and MLXLanguageModel run local models). A monitor can develop against SystemLanguageModel and make cloud a user-chosen option. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-08)

When mDNSResponder gets DoH/DoT designated-resolver info for the current network, it upgrades automatically and the traffic bypasses an active NEDNSProxyProvider; the proxy never sees those queries. Fleet cites Apple feedback FB11963304 as confirming this is intended. DoH on port 443 is indistinguishable from normal HTTPS, so a monitor may report zero DNS activity. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-15)

Apple's own evaluation shows the on-device model beating Qwen-2.5-3B across languages and competitive with Qwen-3-4B and Gemma-3-4B in English, with a ~4.6% MGSM regression from compression; quality is mid-size-open-model level, below cloud frontier models for reasoning over large contexts. (medium confidence)

API keys come in two types: Team keys (all apps, role-based, created by an Admin) and Individual keys (inherit one user's apps and roles). Individual keys cannot use Provisioning endpoints, Sales and Finance, or notaryTool. The private .p8 downloads once only; never commit it. (high confidence)

fastlane recommends a Team key (required for provisioning-related API access); credentials are key_id, issuer_id and the .p8 content, JWT duration max 1200 seconds. fastlane produce has only partial API-key support, pem is Apple ID only, precheck cannot check IAPs with API keys. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)
Apple rejects JWTs with lifetime over 20 minutes for most requests; responses carry an X-Rate-Limit header with an hourly rolling limit, so throttle polling and back off. (medium confidence)

A Private app cannot be changed to Public (and Public cannot become Private); changing requires a new app record. Public can later become Unlisted after approval via an Apple request. (high confidence)

An independent arXiv audit (24 Aug 2026) of SystemLanguageModel.default found it confabulated confidently on 69.1% of false-premise questions, refused 18.4% of benign summarization inputs (peers 0%), and had verbalized confidence near 99% with chance-level AUROC 0.47. A diagnosis feature should not present model output as authoritative; ground it in measured data and let deterministic code decide pass/fail. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-24)

Enforcement timeline for the platforms that are covered: warning emails from 2024-03-13, App Store Connect rejection of missing declarations from 2024-05-01 (ITMS-91053). Invalid manifests (unexpected keys or values) are rejected on any platform, with an email naming the bad file path. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

If NSPrivacyTracking is true, domains in NSPrivacyTrackingDomains fail with an error when the user has not granted ATT permission. A DNS/network monitor that surfaces tracker domains is not itself tracking, so it should set NSPrivacyTracking false unless it really tracks. (medium confidence)

WWDC26 adds PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel behind the same session API: 32,000-token context, reasoning levels (.light/.deep), no account or API key, prompts not stored, free for developers under 2 million first-time downloads with higher daily limits for iCloud+ users. It is a cloud call, so it needs the network and its privacy claim is Apple's PCC guarantee rather than on-device. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-08)

The older single-call /appStoreVersionSubmissions endpoint is described as gone/replaced by reviewSubmissions; Apple's own deprecation notice was not retrievable, so confirm against the OpenAPI spec. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

Search reports state no API exists for the App Privacy questionnaire (manual in the web UI) while age ratings are automatable via ageRatingDeclarations; treat as unverified against Apple docs. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

Apple's release feed lists App Store Connect API 4.5 (22 Sep 2026) as latest; 4.3.1 shipped 12 May 2026. Individual API keys reportedly landed May 2026 per search summary of a Fivetran changelog, not Apple. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22)

Private distribution (Custom Apps) is chosen in App Store Connect under Pricing and Availability > App Distribution Methods > Private, restricted to specified Organization IDs (or Apple Accounts for legacy VPP). Distribution is via MDM or redemption codes. (high confidence)

Custom apps go through standard App Review (typically 1-2 days); apps needing login must supply sample data/authentication to reviewers. Customer organizations must enable Custom Apps in settings, then find the app under Custom Apps in Apps and Books. (high confidence)
Customer admins find their Organization ID in Apple Business/School Manager under Preferences > Enrollment Information; the developer must collect it to target them. (medium confidence)

Apple announced Apple Business on 2026-03-24 and launched it 2026-04-14, merging Business Manager, Business Essentials and Business Connect into one free platform with built-in MDM in 200+ countries; Apple's own custom-apps guide is now titled 'Apple Business'. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-14)

Third-party MDMs (e.g. Intune) sync custom apps through location tokens (legacy VPP tokens), valid one year; a token works with one MDM at a time; device licensing (default for new Intune assignments) installs via MDM only without App Store sign-in; user licensing covers up to 5 devices per Apple Account. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-28)

On macOS, revoking a VPP license leaves the app usable but un-updatable; Apple removes it after a 30-day grace period. Reusing a token on another MDM can lose license assignment records. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-28)

Intune VPP tokens can use DDM management (iOS/iPadOS 18+) but DDM supports only Required/Uninstall, not Available; keep MDM for Available assignments and app-config policies. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-28)

A developer forum report shows a custom app assigned by device license failing on macOS InstallApplication with AMSErrorDomain code 301 'Invalid Status Code'; filed as FB11292074, no documented resolution (2022-era, example used iOS ID). (low confidence)

The Foundation Models framework exposes Apple's roughly 3-billion-parameter on-device model to apps through a Swift API; it runs offline and Apple states it is designed for summarization, entity extraction, text understanding, refinement and short dialog, not as a general world-knowledge chatbot. (high confidence)

The WWDC26 release ships a rebuilt on-device model, better at logic and tool calling and with vision input; the session example prints model.contextSize as 8192 and adds model.tokenCount(for:) so an app can budget instructions and prompts. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-08)

The original (2025) on-device model had a fixed 4096-token context window shared by instructions, prompt, tool schemas and response; exceeding it throws GenerationError.exceededContextWindowSize. A raw DNS or connection log therefore has to be pre-aggregated in app code before it reaches the model. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-08)

On-device inference keeps prompt and response data on the Mac, so hostnames, IPs and resolver config in a diagnosis prompt are not sent to a third party; this is the privacy advantage over a cloud AI call. Apple also states it does not train on users' private personal data or interactions. (high confidence)

WWDC26 adds an fm command-line tool (macOS 27), a Python SDK, an Evaluations framework to measure feature quality, and open-sources the framework; the Evaluations framework is the sanctioned way to test diagnosis prompt quality before shipping. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-08)

Since iOS 16 / macOS Ventura, devices automatically upgrade to encrypted DNS via Discovery of Designated Resolvers (DDR): on joining a network the device issues an SVCB query for _dns.resolver.arpa and, if answered, uses TLS or HTTPS. DDR applies to one network at a time and does not work if the resolver has a private IP address. (high confidence)

System-wide encrypted DNS can be configured manually with NEDNSSettingsManager in an app or a DNSSettings profile payload; individual apps can opt in with PrivacyContext on NWParameters. Client certificate auth via identityReference on NEDNSSettings is supported since iOS 16 / macOS Ventura. (high confidence)

macOS 27 adds a DNS settings declarative (DDM) configuration for DoH (RFC 8484 URI template) or DoT (hostname), with optional supplemental match domains, failover to system DNS, client certificates and on-demand rules. It does not require supervision but requires MDM with Device Enrollment or Automated Device Enrollment (not User Enrollment). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

At WWDC26 Apple moved network configurations, including DNS Proxy and DNS Settings, to declarative device management for OS 27, with public release expected fall 2026. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-11)

On macOS 26.6.1, a network advertising DoT/DoH via DHCP DNR/DDR (RFC 9463/9462) made mDNSResponder send all queries, including local and split-DNS names, to the network's DoH resolver, overriding Tailscale DNS; scutil --dns still showed the configured servers, so 'dig works, apps don't'. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-15)

After macOS 26.1 (reports from 2025-11-09), installing encrypted-DNS .mobileconfig files fails with 'The "VPN Service" payload could not be installed. The VPN service could not be created.' even though the profile has only a DNS Settings payload. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-11-10)

Mitigations for DNS visibility under encrypted DNS include using resolvers without DoH/DoT, answering _dns.resolver.arpa with NXDOMAIN, forcing a corporate encrypted resolver, firewalling known DoH IPs, SNI inspection, or a TLS-intercepting proxy; all are enterprise-side measures unavailable to a sandboxed App Store app. (low confidence)

Apple's required-reason API documentation says to describe reasons for apps and SDKs 'on iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS, or watchOS'; macOS is not in that list. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

The privacy manifest page splits scope: collected-data-type declarations are required on all platforms; required-reasons API declarations only on iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

Independent developers reached the same reading: SwiftLee (2024-04-30): 'As of now, an API declaration is not required for macOS'; the .NET blog (2024-03-25) says macOS and Mac Catalyst do not seem to need required-reason entries; a 2026-09-05 project issue closed with macOS excluded from required-reason platforms. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-05)

On macOS and Mac Catalyst the app manifest goes in Contents/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy; macOS framework manifests go in Versions/A/Resources/. iOS-family apps use the bundle root. The file name PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy is mandatory. (high confidence)

Required-reason categories: FileTimestamp (stat, fstat, lstat, getattrlist family; codes DDA9.1 display to user, C617.1 app container, 3B52.1 user-granted files, 0A2A.1 SDK wrapper), SystemBootTime (mach_absolute_time; 35F9.1, 8FFB.1, 3D61.1), DiskSpace (statfs/statvfs family; 85F4.1, E174.1, 7D9E.1, B728.1), plus UserDefaults and ActiveKeyboard. Each has off-device-transmission limits. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

Apple says it reviews the required-reason API list and reasons continually and updates the article from time to time, so macOS scope could change; declaring accurate reasons anyway is low cost for a monitor that uses stat or mach_absolute_time. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

Apple's third-party SDK list (80+ SDKs, e.g. Firebase, Alamofire, Flutter, Realm) requires a privacy manifest plus a signature for binary dependencies, checked on App Store Connect submissions from 2025-02-12; a monitor app that bundles such SDKs must pick up versions that comply. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

Declared reasons bind behavior: data from these APIs may be used only for the declared reason, must match functionality shown to users, and may not be used for fingerprinting or tracking; most reasons forbid sending derived data off-device. (high confidence)
